title: Zero-Field Long Range Order at $T \sim 40$ mK in the Proximate Quantum Spin Ice Ce$_2$Sn$_2$O$_7$ and Phase Diagram for Magnetic Fields Along [1,1,0]
authors: E. M. Smith, M. S. Powell, R. Schäfer, A. P. Dioguardi, J. W. Kolis, R. Movshovich, B. D. Gaulin
abstract: The Ce$^{3+}$ pseudospin-1/2 degrees of freedom in the pyrochlore magnets Ce$_2$X$_2$O$_7$, with $X$ = Zr, Hf, or Sn, possess dipole-octupole character. The XYZ nearest-neighbor model Hamiltonians which have successfully described their properties make them attractive candidates for quantum spin ice ground states. We report new heat capacity measurements to very low temperatures on a high-quality single crystal of Ce$_2$Sn$_2$O$_7$ grown by hydrothermal techniques. Our zero-field measurements uncover a clear first order transition to long-ranged order at $T \sim 0.04$ K, well below the downturn in the broader Schottky-like anomaly that is a common feature in the zero-field heat capacity for cerium pyrochlores. This observation settles the debate as to whether Ce$_2$Sn$_2$O$_7$ possesses a QSI ground state in zero field - it does not. However, we also find compelling evidence suggesting that spin ice physics is nearby, and remains relevant to Ce$_2$Sn$_2$O$_7$. Application of a magnetic field along the $[1,1,0]$ direction leads to an evolution of this peak to a weak anomaly at higher temperature more characteristic of a continuous, mean field transition. At higher fields along $[1,1,0]$, the Schottky-like anomaly bifurcates similar to expectations for independent polarized $α$ and orthogonal $β$ chains in classical spin ice. These new experimental results demonstrate richness to the phase diagram for Ce-based pyrochlores.
summary: This study investigates the magnetic ground state of $	ext{Ce}_2	ext{Sn}_2	ext{O}_7$ using ultra-low temperature heat capacity measurements. The results show a distinct first-order transition at $T \sim 0.04$ K, ruling out a Quantum Spin Ice ground state in zero field. Furthermore, applying a magnetic field reveals the underlying physics by splitting excitations into two characteristic chains ($\alpha$ and $ eta$), providing a detailed phase diagram.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the ground state of $	ext{Ce}_2	ext{Sn}_2	ext{O}_7$ and characterize its magnetic ordering transition in zero field and under an applied magnetic field.
main_result: Zero-field heat capacity measurements reveal a clear first-order transition to long-ranged order at $T \sim 0.04$ K, indicating the material does not possess a Quantum Spin Ice ground state. However, applying a magnetic field along [1,1,0] causes the anomaly to bifurcate into features characteristic of independent $\alpha$ and $ eta$ chains.
method: The research combines low-temperature heat capacity measurements ($C_{	ext{mag}}$) with theoretical modeling using nearest-neighbor XYZ Hamiltonians and Linked Cluster expansions (NLC).
model_or_system: The system is the pyrochlore magnet $	ext{Ce}_2	ext{Sn}_2	ext{O}_7$, whose magnetic moments are modeled by pseudospin-1/2 degrees of freedom. The interactions are described by an XYZ nearest-neighbor Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Zero-field heat capacity anomaly ($T_N \sim 0.04$ K), Schottky anomalies under field, and entropy recovery plateaus ($\propto R/2 \ln(2)$).
important_parameters: Transition temperature $T_N \sim 0.04$ K; magnetic field direction [1,1,0]; coupling parameters $(J_a, J_b, J_c)$.
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes the applicability of the XYZ Hamiltonian and models the high-field behavior by decomposing the lattice into $\alpha$ and $ eta$ chains.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate $C_{	ext{mag}}(T)$ vs. field, showing the zero-field transition and its evolution/bifurcation under a [1,1,0] field; phase diagrams map this field dependence; residual plots ($\delta^2$) confirm model agreement.
paper_structure: The paper progresses from initial zero-field measurements establishing magnetic ordering ($T \sim 0.04$ K), to analyzing the effect of an external magnetic field along [1,1,0] which reveals chain decomposition and Schottky anomalies, concluding with detailed theoretical fitting using NLC methods.
why_interesting: The work provides a crucial experimental test case for understanding the transition between highly frustrated quantum spin ice states and conventional magnetically ordered states in pyrochlores, relevant to many-body physics models.
